I can search for more specific dates but the timeline is that I was hired as a web intern in 2011 and I kept getting extended until the next year in 2012 and I was hired as a web producer. Then I worked that position until November 2014 when I started on the Tigers beat.
From: Stevie Blanchard <stevie@detroitguild22.org>
Sent: Wednesday, July 22, 2020 11:12 AM
To: Fenech, Anthony <afenech@freepress.com>
Subject: Re: Pizza-gate 
 
This is helpful. Can you tell me when your start date and original title was and when you started the Tigers beat?
I have a call out to Peter but haven't heard back.

On Tue, Jul 21, 2020, 4:32 PM Fenech, Anthony <afenech@freepress.com> wrote:
Here is information on our correspondence yesterday. I have not spoken to Peter about any of this.

Chris Thomas texted me at 4:09 p.m. yesterday saying, “Hey, Anthony: Ron says someone had Jets delivered to the stadium today in his name. I trust this wasn’t us, right?”
I said, “Yes, I ordered two pizzas, a Jet’s bread and a two-liter of Coke for the Tigers media relations department fo ra job well done this summer.”
Thomas sent two texts, “Did you tell them you were doing it?” and “And why would you do that after the issues the other day without talking to them?” I said, “No, I didn’t tell them.”

I spoke on the phone with Thomas later in the afternoon around 5 p.m. and he asked me to explain why I sent the Tigers pizza.
I told him that I thought they did a good job with summer camp and that I understood that it may have been taken as bad humor but I was trying to apologize for the situation on July 5.
Asked why I would do it by sending the same thing that they didn’t want in the clubhouse, I said that I was not intending for the pizza to be delivered to the clubhouse.
I told him my intention, as a nice gesture, was to send him pizza for doing a good job this summer.
Told the Tigers have a strict rule against communal food, I said I was aware of the media regulations about bringing food into the ballpark but I did not know anything about the team’s internal policy about communal food and furthermore, I was not bringing food into the ballpark.
Thomas said that he thought it was petty and I said that I sent them pizza.
Thomas said the Tigers were sensitive about this issue and that it was a serious thing. 
I told Thomas that I put Colangelo’s name and number down as the delivery contact. Asked why I did not tell Colangelo first, I told Thomas that I had intended to tell Colangelo about it but the team announced a flurry of roster moves and the general manager was speaking to the media after the workout leading up to the expected delivery time of 3-3:15 p.m. I told Thomas that I was intending on letting Colangelo know but I was working.
Thomas said, “Part of me wants to stop this, it’s always something.” and said he would call me back.

I spoke on the phone with Thomas again around 6 p.m. and said that the situation was an intentional thing to throw it in Ron’s face or an incredible lack of judgment and that either way, he’s done with it.
He said that effective now, I’m on the web desk and we’ll evaluate from there. 
When I asked him why I was being re-assigned to the web desk, Thomas said, “Because I can’t trust that you will do the right things and in a very, very strict environment.”
Thomas said that I did the same thing after we previously spoke about the issue on July 15 and that the judgment was poor. 
Thomas said that he wanted to move me to the web desk and we’re going to figure out things. “If we get comfortable then we can re-think it,” he said. Thomas said that was the decision they’re making and going forward with.
I reiterated my explanation of the situation and that I was planning on telling Colangelo about the delivery. 
Thomas asked me how I expected Colangelo to react to this and I said I thought it was a nice gesture to send them pizza, that I did not bring it into the stadium as a member of the credentialed media and that they didn’t have any obligation to take the pizza. 
Thomas said he would send me a note later on but “Effective now, you’re going to the desk and we will figure out where we go.”
Last night, Thomas sent me this e-mail:

Anthony: Just following up on our conversation earlier. 
Starting Tuesday, you’re reassigned to the web desk. The duties include, but are not limited to, writing breaking news, editing, building galleries, publishing video, or anything else we need help with. 
You can work remotely. 
I’ve got you scheduled noon-8 p.m. from Tuesday-Friday. I’ll evaluate next week’s schedule later this week. 
Kirk will follow up with more details tomorrow. If there’s a reason the schedule doesn’t work this week, please let Kirk know and he can adjust it to what works best for him. Otherwise, be on Teams and ready to roll at noon. 
Thanks.
I said, “OK, cool. Thank you. Anthony.”
